To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified three members of the neuronal acetylcholine nicotinic receptor-related gene family, that these three genes form a gene cluster, and that they are expressed in both the PC12 cell lines and in the rat brain.

we have identified two new members of the nAChRs-related gene family, the genes encoding these two new proteins, alpha 5 and alpha 4, and the gene encoding beta 4, form a tightly linked cluster, and these three new genes are expressed in a small number nuclei in the rat brain.
(i) we have identified a new member of the nACh receptor gene family, the alpha 5 gene, and (ii) we have shown that the beta 4 gene forms a gene cluster with the alpha 3 and alpha 5 genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genes encoding the alpha 5, beta 4, and beta 5 nAChR proteins.
the molecular cloning and characterization of genes encoding nAChR-like proteins.
the molecular characterization of a family of nAChR genes.

the alpha 5, alpha 3 and alpha 4 genes are transcribed with the same polarity and form a tightly clustered gene cluster spanning approximately sixty base pairs.
alpha 3, alpha5, and beta4 are the members of the rat nAChRs gene family.

we have isolated and characterized three new members of the nAChRs-related gene family.
the rat nAChRs are encoded by at least 12 distinct genes.

we have identified three new members of the neuronal nAChR family of genes.

we have identified two additional genes encoding neuronal nAChR-like subunits, alpha 5 and alpha 4, which are members of a gene family that includes alpha 1, alpha 2, alpha 3 and alpha 5, beta 1, beta 2, and beta 3.
